claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a homogenized, single-phase BCC alloy in the proposed initial state.
Atomic-size mismatch in HfNbTaTiZr produces pronounced local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions generate heterogeneous internal stress fields.
At room temperature, these internal stress fields resist deformation.
Heating HfNbTaTiZr to 600–900 °C increases atomic-vibration amplitudes and partially relaxes its local lattice distortions.
Relaxation of local lattice distortions lowers the barrier to dislocation slip.
Elevated temperature facilitates activation of multiple {110} or non-traditional slip systems.
Many small slips can occur on multiple {110} planes in a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
Relative to room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr will have lower yield strength at 600–900 °C.
Relative to room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower Young’s modulus at 600–900 °C.
Activation of multiple slip systems at elevated temperature will increase the ductility of HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a non-linear, enhanced thermal-expansion coefficient in the 600–900 °C range.
Temperature-dependent relaxation of lattice distortion is the common cause of the predicted decreases in yield strength and modulus and the non-linear thermal expansion.
The 600–900 °C interval is below the onset of microstructural degradation or phase transformation in the tested HfNbTaTiZr state.
Precipitation, phase transformations, dynamic recrystallization, or diffusion-driven transformations can dominate elevated-temperature mechanical behavior outside the stated regime.
Comparable moderate strain rates will allow thermally activated mechanisms to dominate.
At room temperature, the local lattice distortions are fully intact.
High-temperature XRD and TEM can be used to track lattice-parameter changes, local lattice strain, slip-system activity, and dislocation behavior during testing.

contradictions.description: The mechanism requires temperature-induced relaxation of local lattice strain, but the falsification rule lists 'unchanged local lattice strain' as an example of evidence of relaxed lattice distortions. Unchanged strain would instead oppose the proposed mediator.

Phase transformation or degradation is defined as outside the hypothesis's validity domain, yet its occurrence is also said to falsify the hypothesis. An out-of-domain result is normally an exclusion or boundary failure rather than a decisive test of the in-domain mechanism.
